claude.rationale: This is a whole-company going-private acquisition: Sub merged into West, West survived intact as a wholly owned subsidiary, and "the whole going-concern business (all four reportable segments) transferred to Parent's ownership as a single unit" with no divestiture, carve-out, or spin-off. Product (T4) and the operating processes (T5) moved together as an undivided going concern, so gap_45 = 0. The surviving corporation assumed, honored, and continued West's existing employment, severance, retention, and executive change-in-control arrangements, so processes and the people/organization (T6) transferred coherently together, giving gap_56 = 0. T1 = replace because merger consideration was all-cash with no pre-merger stockholder (including founders) retaining any interest, installing Apollo funds as the new controlling principal.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company acquisition where the entire entity, including all segments, products, processes, and people, transferred intact to the new owner. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch between products and processes (gap_45 = 0) or between processes and people (gap_56 = 0) at closing.

openai.rationale: The product/business-model line states that the whole going concern, including all four reportable segments, transferred as a single unit without a divestiture, carve-out, or spin-off, while the structural summary states that the target survived intact; therefore, no product-versus-process mismatch at closing is documented [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-215084, DEFM14A]. The processes/people lines state that existing employment, severance, retention, termination, and executive arrangements continued, with pre-merger service credited, so the operating substrate was accompanied by the organization that ran it and no T5–T6 gap is documented [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-215084, DEFM14A].
